keywords: how are chinos supposed to fit
answer: Chinos fit when the waist sits flat without a belt doing the work, the seat is smooth with no sagging, you can pinch about ½–1 in of fabric at the thigh, the leg tapers cleanly from knee to ankle, and the hem has little or no break, just touching the top of your shoe.
intro: Chinos sit between jeans and dress trousers, so they should look trimmer than jeans but more relaxed than suit pants. Cotton twill wrinkles and creases where it's too tight and bags where it's too loose, so the fabric shows a bad fit quickly. Check them standing, sitting and walking.

checklist.good: Lies flat and stays up on its own with one to two fingers of room. A belt is for looks, not to hold them up.
checklist.tooTight: The button pulls, the waistband rolls over, or the zip area creases into horizontal folds.
checklist.tooLoose: The waistband gaps at the back or you need to cinch a belt so the fabric gathers.

checklist.good: Mid-rise is typical, sitting just below the navel. The crotch sits close without pulling and you can sit without the back dropping.
checklist.tooTight: The crotch seam presses up or creates smile-shaped creases at the front.
checklist.tooLoose: Extra fabric hangs below the fly and the crotch sits low.

checklist.good: Follows your shape without clinging. The back pockets lie flat.
checklist.tooTight: The pockets pull open and horizontal creases form across the seat.
checklist.tooLoose: Fabric droops and folds below the seat.

checklist.good: About ½–1 in of fabric to pinch at the front of the thigh. Front pockets lie closed.
checklist.tooTight: The front pockets flare and the twill shows strain lines across the thigh.
checklist.tooLoose: Fabric balloons around the thigh and folds when you stand.

checklist.good: The leg narrows gently from the knee to the ankle with no twisting.
checklist.tooTight: The fabric clings to the calf and wrinkles behind the knee.
checklist.tooLoose: The lower leg is so wide it flaps when you walk and hides your shoes.

checklist.good: No break or a slight break: the hem just touches or barely rests on the top of the shoe. Rolled or cropped chinos end at the ankle bone.
checklist.tooTight: Too short: several inches of sock show when standing, unless you're going for a deliberate crop.
checklist.tooLoose: Too long: fabric stacks into folds over the shoes, which looks sloppier in chinos than in jeans.

variations.heading: Slim, straight and relaxed chinos
variations.intro: Pick the cut by build and how dressy you want to look. The waist and seat should fit the same in each.

items.name: Slim fit
items.text: The most common modern chino. Close through the thigh and tapered at the ankle, worn with no break or a slight break. Suits slim and average builds.

items.name: Athletic or tapered
items.text: More room in the seat and thigh, then a strong taper below the knee. A good fit for muscular legs that strain slim chinos.

items.name: Straight or classic
items.text: An even leg from knee to hem. Looks more traditional and suits larger builds; wear with a slight break.

items.name: Relaxed and pleated
items.text: Fuller cut, sometimes with pleats and a higher rise. Pleats should lie closed when standing. These suit a looser, more casual outfit and wider shoes.

items.name: Women's chinos
items.text: Usually cut slim, straight or wide, often at ankle length. The same waist, seat and thigh checks apply; ankle-length styles should end at or just above the ankle bone.

measure.heading: How to size chinos
measure.intro: Chinos are usually sold by waist and inseam, like jeans, but cotton twill has less give than denim.
steps: Measure your waist where you'll wear the chinos, usually just below the navel, keeping the tape snug and level.
Measure the inseam of a pair of pants that fits you well, from the crotch seam to the hem along the inside leg.
If the chinos are 100% cotton, expect them to soften but not stretch much; buy the size that is comfortable when buttoned.
If they contain elastane, expect them to give a little during the day, so a snugger fit is fine.
Compare the brand's garment measurements, especially thigh and leg opening, with pants you already like.
measure.tip: Many brands also preshrink their chinos, but untreated cotton can shrink slightly in a hot wash or dryer. Wash cold and hang dry to keep the length you bought.

problems.problem: Chinos crease heavily at the crotch and lap
problems.fix: They're too tight or the rise is too short. Go up a size or choose a cut with more thigh and seat room.

problems.problem: Too long and stacking on the shoe
problems.fix: Hem them for no break or a slight break. Rolling the cuff works for casual wear but bulky rolls make the leg look shorter.

problems.problem: Fit at the waist but tight in the thigh
problems.fix: Try an athletic or tapered fit at the same waist size rather than sizing up and taking in the waist.

problems.problem: Chinos stretched out and sag by evening
problems.fix: Stretch chinos with a high elastane content can bag. Size down, or choose a lower-stretch twill that recovers better.

problems.problem: Leg too wide below the knee
problems.fix: A tailor can taper the leg from the knee to the hem, which is a common, inexpensive alteration.

extra.heading: Chinos vs jeans vs dress pants
extra.body: Chinos should fit a little cleaner than jeans: less stack at the hem and a smoother seat, because twill shows wrinkles more. Compared with dress trousers, chinos usually sit a bit lower, are cut slimmer, and are worn with less break. If you wear your chinos with a blazer, aim for no break or a slight break so the hem looks deliberate.

extra.heading: Cuffing and rolling
extra.body: A neat single or double roll of about 1–1½ in works with sneakers, loafers and boat shoes, especially in summer. Roll only if the leg is tapered; on wide legs it adds bulk. For dressier looks, hem chinos at the right length instead of rolling.

picks.label: Slim-fit stretch chinos
picks.why: A little elastane makes a slim cut comfortable to sit in all day.

picks.label: Athletic-fit chinos
picks.why: Extra seat and thigh room for muscular builds without a baggy lower leg.

picks.label: Women's ankle-length chinos
picks.why: Pre-cropped length that works with flats and sneakers, no hemming needed for most heights.

faqs.q: Should chinos be tight or loose?
faqs.a: Trim but not tight. You should be able to pinch about ½–1 in of fabric at the thigh, sit without strain, and see a clean line from knee to ankle.
Long enough to just touch the top of your shoe, with no break or a slight break. Chinos look best shorter than jeans.
A gentle taper from knee to ankle suits most people and keeps the hem from swallowing your shoes. Very wide legs look more casual.
Cotton chinos soften but don't stretch much. Chinos with elastane loosen a little through the day, so you can buy them snug.

faqs.q: Should I size down in chinos?
faqs.a: Usually not, unless they're stretchy. Buy the size that buttons comfortably and fits the seat, then hem or taper as needed.
Waist flat without relying on a belt, smooth seat, a little fabric to pinch at the thigh, a tapered leg and a hem with little or no break.
